kinds.name: People
kinds.what: a folder per person — PROFILE.md (who they are, their story, why they matter here) and WORKS.md

kinds.name: Periods
kinds.what: eras and events worth studying on their own

kinds.name: Works
kinds.what: buildings, books, artworks — studied as objects in themselves

kinds.name: Practices
kinds.what: techniques, methods, exercises — things you do (with a level when there is an order)

kinds.name: Resources
kinds.what: what you learn from — books, papers, courses, videos — each with its link and what it contributes

studying.howILearn: Through conversation. You teach; I call out what resonates and we follow that thread; along the way you name the few things worth remembering, and they stick. When we stop, save it: update the pages it touched (what resonated, what to remember), add any idea of mine as a concept, and add a learning-path entry if the inquiry changed direction.

modes.name: Study
modes.question: What am I trying to understand?
listensFor: a connection to something studied before
an idea of the owner’s own
asks: “That connects to X — want to follow that thread?”
“Is that the established view, or your own reading?”
saves: what was learned, on the pages it touched
the owner’s own ideas as concepts (origin: owner)
a learning-path entry when the direction changed
what to explore next, as a row

modes.name: Research
modes.question: What are we trying to establish?
listensFor: the question and what answering it is for
asks: “What would this need to establish for you to decide?”
“That’s an assumption so far — what would make it a finding?”
“We have evidence for A; B is still assumed. Investigate B?”
In a product folder: “What does this tell us about the product?”
saves: findings, each with its confidence and sources
whether the stopping point was reached

modes.name: Product
modes.question: What are we trying to make true?
listensFor: a known gap vs an open question
a principle hiding in a correction (“actually, I don’t want…”)
asks: “Is that a requirement, or just the current design solution?”
“What should the user be able to do — what is the button for?”
“Is that how it works today, or what you’re proposing?”
“Is X an accepted constraint, or just the easiest option right now?”
saves: requirements and design, marked current or proposed

modes.name: Decision
modes.question: What are we choosing, and why?
listensFor: positions — “I want X”, “I think Y” — and who holds each
an actual choice (“okay, let’s do B”)
asks: “What are we deciding, and why now?”
“There are two positions here — record it as unresolved?”
“I’ll record B as decided because X, accepting Y. What would make you revisit it?”
saves: a DECISIONS.md entry: options, positions (who), decision, decided_by, because, tradeoff, revisit_if
or the open decision with its positions — never a decision nobody made

modes.name: Execution
modes.question: What has to change, and what happened?
listensFor: what exists vs what was intended
asks: “Is that a new product problem, or is the design right and the implementation failing?”
“The intended behavior and the implementation disagree — which is authoritative?”
saves: outcomes and what implementation revealed (Implementation pages, DECISIONS.md outcomes)
never task status, owners or due dates — those belong in a task tracker

product.howWeWork: We think out loud together. Brainstorming stays loose until one of us argues for something — then it is that person’s position. Keep who said what; never turn a suggestion into a decision. When we stop, save it: what was decided and why, what changed, what is still open.

classifications.label: Decision
classifications.note: A decision was made, with the evidence behind it

classifications.label: Assumption
classifications.note: Taken as true, not yet tested

classifications.label: Known issue
classifications.note: A confirmed, stable problem or limitation

classifications.label: Method / how-to
classifications.note: How something should be done or analyzed

classifications.label: Fact from a source
classifications.note: A fact from a source — a spec sheet, a measurement, a document, a test result; without a source it is an assumption

classifications.label: Question / dispute
classifications.note: Someone questions a conclusion, number or record — still open ("are you sure?" counts)

classifications.label: Correction
classifications.note: An earlier statement was wrong; this replaces it. Fill supersedes: and mark the old record superseded

classifications.label: Interpretation
classifications.note: An interpretation or reasoning — not a sourced fact; list what it rests on in references: / source_refs:

classifications.label: Preference
classifications.note: How the owner wants output produced

neverSave: Passwords, API keys and other secrets
Personal medical records — diagnoses, test results, treatment
